title: Binary derived open descent for modules on a ringed topos
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a Grothendieck topos (a category of sheaves of sets on a small site), $R$ a commutative ring object of $\mathcal T$, and $D(\mathcal T,R)$ the ordinary derived category of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $U,V\hookrightarrow1$ be subterminal objects (monomorphisms into the terminal object) whose union is $1$, and put $W=U\times V$. Write $\mathcal T/U$, $\mathcal T/V$, $\mathcal T/W$ for the slice topoi, $R_U,R_V,R_W$ for the restricted rings, and $j_Z^*$ for restriction to a slice. The exact extension-by-zero left adjoint is denoted $j_{Z!}$ and the derived right adjoint of restriction is denoted $Rj_{Z*}$, for $Z=U,V,W$.

(1) Given $A\in D(\mathcal T/U,R_U)$, $B\in D(\mathcal T/V,R_V)$ and an isomorphism $c:A|_W\xrightarrow{\sim}B|_W$, there exist $G\in D(\mathcal T,R)$ and isomorphisms $a:G|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}A$, $b:G|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ with $b|_W=c\circ a|_W$. One may take $G$ in a distinguished triangle
$$G\longrightarrow Rj_{U*}A\oplus Rj_{V*}B\xrightarrow{(Rj_*c,-1)}Rj_{W*}(B|_W)\longrightarrow G[1],$$
where each component is the derived restriction-adjunction map, with $c$ applied in the first component. If $A,B$ have cohomology in a common interval $[a_0,b_0]$, so does $G$.

(2) For every $M\in D(\mathcal T,R)$ there is the natural distinguished open-cover triangle
$$j_{W!}(M|_W)\xrightarrow{(1,-1)}j_{U!}(M|_U)\oplus j_{V!}(M|_V)\xrightarrow{(1,1)}M\longrightarrow j_{W!}(M|_W)[1].$$
The arrows are the canonical nested-open maps and the adjunction counits. Restriction and extension by zero here act termwise on complexes. No uniqueness of a gluing of arbitrary derived morphisms is asserted.

source.place: Tag 08DG (lemma-glue), first assertion and its Rj_* cone construction; Tag 08BU (lemma-exact-sequence-lower-shriek). The ringed-space arguments are to be extended to open subtopoi of a ringed Grothendieck topos; this extension is the agent-stated prerequisite, not a claim that these tags already state it.

proof.text: Use the fixed termwise restriction and adjunction-map interface. Exact restriction commutes with derived homology via the exact-functor homology comparison.

For a module sheaf vanishing on U and V, a section on any object restricts to zero on the sieve obtained by pulling back the terminal binary cover. Separatedness makes it zero. Apply this after the derived-homology comparison to detect vanishing of derived homology.

For A,B,c define d as the biproduct difference of the canonical nested adjunction maps, with RW(c) on the A component. Complete d to a distinguished fibre triangle using the pretriangulated cocone axiom.
Apply the fibre-restriction theorem to obtain invertible U and V restriction/project/counit maps; use asIso to obtain the required a,b.

Naturality and the adjunction Hom-equivalence identify the transpose of each projected counit with f followed by its nested mate. Transpose the equation f≫d=0 under adjW; additivity gives exactly the stated overlap equation.
Outside a common cohomological interval, a,b and exact restriction imply that H^q(G) vanishes on U and V. The separatedness zero test proves its global vanishing.
Apply the independent natural lower-shriek triangle theorem to obtain the second clause with exactly the required natural delta and its canonical first two arrows.

            compV.hom.app G ≫ rVW.map b.hom) ∧

            IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj A)) →
          (∀ q : ℤ, q < a₀ ∨ b₀ < q →
            IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj B)) →
          ∀ q : ℤ, q < a₀ ∨ b₀ < q →
            IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj G))) ∧
    (∃ (delta : 𝟭 _ ⟶ rW ⋙ lW ⋙ shiftFunctor _ (1 : ℤ)),
      ∀ (M : DerivedCategory (ringedSiteModules.{max u v r}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R))),
        Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk
            (biprod.lift
              ((bangAdjW.homEquiv (rW.obj M) (lU.obj (rU.obj M))).symm
                (compU.hom.app M ≫ rUW.map (bangAdjU.unit.app (rU.obj M)) ≫
                  compU.inv.app (lU.obj (rU.obj M))))

                (compV.hom.app M ≫ rVW.map (bangAdjV.unit.app (rV.obj M)) ≫
